walkthrough: Recall from Lesson 4 that velocity is the gradient of a displacement-time graph.

hints: Direction changes when velocity crosses zero.
Starting at -4.0 m s^-1, a rise of 4.0 m s^-1 is needed to reach zero.
walkthrough: Direction changes when velocity crosses zero.
Starting at -4.0 m s^-1, a rise of 4.0 m s^-1 is needed to reach zero.
At +2.0 m s^-2 this takes 4.0 / 2.0 = 2.0 s.
Therefore the robot changes direction at 2.0 s.

hints: Start at displacement 0 and plot the calculated boundary points (4.0,12), (6.0,12) and (9.0,-6.0).

walkthrough: Start at displacement 0 and plot the calculated boundary points (4.0,12), (6.0,12) and (9.0,-6.0).
Constant +3.0 m s^-1 gives a straight rising line to 4.0 s.
Zero velocity gives a horizontal line to 6.0 s.
Velocity -6.0 m s^-1 gives a straight falling line with twice the first gradient magnitude.
The falling section loses 12 m in 2.0 s, so it crosses displacement zero at 8.0 s before reaching -6.0 m.
